title: Reproduce Huang's hypercube degree theorem
statement: Reconstruct a proof that every induced subgraph on 2^(n-1)+1 vertices of the n-dimensional hypercube has maximum degree at least sqrt(n), for every integer n >= 1.
status_basis: Huang's proof is explicit; the 2012 open-list entry is superseded. Reproduction is calibration, not a new solution.
plain_summary: More than half of a Boolean cube forces a vertex with many selected neighbors. A published short proof makes this useful for checking whether a research workflow can preserve a theorem's quantifiers and produce a reviewable proof.
assumptions: n is an integer at least 1.
The graph is the undirected n-dimensional binary hypercube with edges at Hamming distance one.
The selected graph is induced and has exactly 2^(n-1)+1 vertices.
Classical real linear algebra, including eigenvalue interlacing, is allowed.
scope: Known-theorem reproduction. First reconstruct the mathematical argument for all n. A formal proof-assistant version is optional and requires a separate environment choice; small numerical checks alone do not complete this task.
target: A self-contained proof document with a dependency ledger; optionally a machine-checked formalization with the same statement.
success_criteria: A specialist accepts the proof with all lemmas and quantifiers explicit.
The induced-subgraph condition and vertex threshold agree with Theorem 1.1.
Any formal artifact declares axioms and dependencies and is checked by an independent trusted kernel.
The result is labeled reproduction throughout.
known_results: Huang's Theorem 1.1 proves this statement; Theorems 1.4–1.5 connect it to sensitivity.
The 2012 problem-list entry is historical evidence, not an open problem to solve again.
significance: A compact cross-domain calibration for proof reconstruction, citation accuracy and statement alignment. Its scientific novelty is zero unless a separately reviewed extension is proposed.

requirements.data: The cited paper and mathematical definitions only; no empirical dataset.
requirements.compute: Symbolic proof first. Optional small matrices grow as 2^n by 2^n; never materialize large cubes merely because no experiment is needed. Formalization cost unknown; no run or time estimate exists.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite simple graphs and classical real linear algebra. Formal foundations and allowed axioms must be recorded if formalized.

ai_assessment.rationale: Useful first calibration because the target and reference proof are explicit and errors can be localized to linear-algebra lemmas. This predicts auditability, not research discovery or model success.

clarity.reason: The graph, threshold and desired bound are fixed.

decomposability.reason: Separate signed-matrix construction, spectrum, interlacing and degree bound.

methods.reason: An accessible primary proof supplies a reference.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Symbolic block-matrix reasoning is useful; brute-force graph search is unnecessary.

checkability.reason: A human can compare a short derivation to the reference theorem.

expertise.reason: Linear algebra and graph-theoretic proof review are needed.

significance.reason: High workflow-calibration value; no new theorem is sought.

verification_difficulty.reason: Submatrix dimensions and eigenvalue ordering are subtle despite a short statement.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model has been tested. Familiarity with the published proof may contaminate any discovery-style benchmark; this is intentionally a reproduction benchmark.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with source retrieval, symbolic reasoning and optional access to a proof assistant.

obstacles: An attractive but wrong eigenvalue-index argument can look convincing.
Checking a few values of n cannot establish a universal theorem.
A formalization can prove a weakened statement if the translation is not audited.

steps: Freeze the reference version and restate all definitions.
Review each lemma independently, especially matrix dimensions and signs.
Check the final statement against Theorem 1.1 rather than the paper's historical conjecture wording.
If formalized, record proof-assistant/library versions and inspect the theorem and axioms after kernel checking.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate; a reviewer needs spectral graph theory or linear algebra. Automated acceptance alone does not validate the source-to-formal-statement translation.
validation.statement_alignment: A proof about non-induced subgraphs, another vertex threshold, or finite tested dimensions is not this task.

known_attempts: Huang 2019 provides the known solution. No project attempt has been made; no specific AI reproduction is claimed.
unresolved_checks: Whether an existing formalization can be reused should be searched before a later attempt.
Choose a proof assistant only if formalization is in scope; no toolchain has been selected.
